- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops 5%+ from recent high, forecast should not rise above 10% above prior low for next 10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment >0.6 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values for next 7–14 days.
